eyebrow: Statistics & Probability for Data Science · Chapter 3, Lesson 11
subtitle: The small family that shows up whenever you count things.

code:
from scipy import stats
b = stats.bernoulli(0.3)
print(b.mean(), round(b.var(), 2))   # 0.3  0.21
caption: Two outcomes, 1 or 0, with success probability p. Mean = p, variance = p(1-p).

code:
binom = stats.binom(10, 0.3)   # 10 orders, 30% return chance
print(round(binom.pmf(3), 4))  # 0.2668 -- exactly 3 returns
print(round(binom.cdf(3), 4))  # 0.6496 -- 3 or fewer
print(round(binom.sf(4), 4))   # 0.1503 -- more than 4 (5+)
caption: Assumes independent trials and a constant p. Clustered returns violate that -- wider real spread.

code:
sim = rng.binomial(10, 0.3, size=100_000)
print(round((sim == 3).mean(), 4))   # 0.2679 -- close to exact 0.2668
caption: Never trust a formula you can't verify. Small gap is simulation noise, not a mistake.

eyebrow: Poisson: events per unit of time
code:
pois = stats.poisson(4)   # help desk averages 4 tickets/hour
print(round(pois.pmf(0), 4))   # 0.0183 -- a silent hour
print(round(pois.pmf(4), 4))   # 0.1954
print(round(pois.sf(7), 4))    # 0.0511 -- 8 or more
caption: Mean = variance = lambda. Overdispersion (variance >> mean) means Poisson is the wrong model.

eyebrow: Poisson is the limit of binomial(huge n, tiny p)
caption: A useful shortcut: when n is huge and p is tiny, Poisson approximates the binomial well.

eyebrow: Geometric: trials until the first success
code:
geo = stats.geom(0.2)   # each visitor converts w.p. 0.2
print(round(geo.pmf(3), 4))   # 0.128 -- first conversion on visitor 3
print(geo.mean())             # 5.0   -- average wait = 1/p
caption: How many trials until the first success? That's geometric.
